# 🚗 Spring Break Family Road Trip: Seattle → San Antonio → Austin → Houston
### April 10–18 | Family of 4 | Budget: $3,000

---

## 1. 🚗 Rental Car

### Recommendation: Mid-Size SUV (e.g., Toyota RAV4, Ford Escape, or similar)

A mid-size SUV is the sweet spot for your family — enough room for 4 passengers plus luggage without paying full-size SUV prices. You'll want the cargo space after shopping on South Congress in Austin.

**Estimated Cost: $420–$560 total (7–8 days)**
- Daily rate: ~$55–$75/day (Spring Break is peak season — rates spike)
- One-way drop fee (SAT → HOU/IAH): Usually $0–$75 with major carriers on this route, but confirm at booking
- Add insurance, taxes, and fees: Budget an additional $80–$120

### Best Rental Companies for This Route
| Company | Notes |
|---------|-------|
| **Enterprise** | Best for one-way Texas routes; often waives drop fees intra-state |
| **National** | Great if you have Emerald Club status; faster pickup |
| **Costco Travel** | Often 10–25% cheaper than booking direct; no drop fee surprises |
| **Autoslash** | Not a rental company — a free tool that monitors your reservation and automatically rebooks if prices drop |

### 💡 Money-Saving Tips
- **Book NOW** — Spring Break is one of the busiest rental periods. Prices rise weekly
- Search **Costco Travel or USAA** (if applicable) before booking direct
- Use **AutoSlash.com** — set it and forget it; it tracks price drops automatically
- Avoid the airport rental counter add-ons (GPS, prepaid gas, toll packages) — use your phone for navigation, pay tolls with cash or a card
- **Skip the rental company's CDW insurance** if your personal auto insurance or credit card covers rentals (call your insurer first to confirm)
- Fill the gas tank yourself before return — prepaid gas is nearly always a rip-off
- Consider dropping at **HOU (Hobby)** rather than IAH — it's slightly closer to Austin and can be cheaper for drop-off fees

---

## 2. 🏨 Hotels

### San Antonio — 3 Nights (April 10–13)
*Target: Near the Riverwalk for walkability and evening atmosphere*

---

#### Option A: 🥇 Best Overall Family Pick
### **Hyatt Regency San Antonio Riverwalk**
- **Price:** ~$180–$220/night → **~$540–$660 for 3 nights**
- **Location:** Directly on the Riverwalk — walk out the back door to the river
- **Pros:**
  - Can't beat the location — zero driving needed for Riverwalk evenings
  - Pool (kids will demand it)
  - Spacious rooms; rollaway beds available
  - Concierge can book River Walk dinner cruises
- **Cons:**
  - Priciest of the three options
  - Parking is $35–$40/night (budget this in)
  - Can feel convention-center busy during Spring Break
- **Why it's great for kids:** The Riverwalk is literally outside the hotel — evening walks to get ice cream or watch the boats become an easy family ritual

---

#### Option B: 💰 Best Value
### **Drury Inn & Suites San Antonio Riverwalk**
- **Price:** ~$140–$170/night → **~$420–$510 for 3 nights**
- **Location:** 2-block walk to the Riverwalk
- **Pros:**
  - **Free hot breakfast included** (huge with kids — saves $60–$80/day easily)
  - Free evening snacks and drinks ("5:30 Kickback") — legitimately good for families
  - Indoor/outdoor pool
  - Self-parking ~$20/night (cheaper than competitors)
  - Drury is consistently rated #1 in guest satisfaction for mid-scale hotels
- **Cons:**
  - Rooms slightly smaller than Hyatt
  - Not directly ON the Riverwalk (2-block walk)
- **Why it's great for kids:** Free breakfast alone makes this the smart budget choice — you'll save $200+ over 3 days versus eating out every morning

> **⭐ This is my top recommendation** for your budget. The free breakfast benefit alone saves ~$200 over 3 days.

---

#### Option C: 🏠 Space for Families
### **Homewood Suites by Hilton San Antonio Riverwalk**
- **Price:** ~$150–$185/night → **~$450–$555 for 3 nights**
- **Location:** 3-4 blocks from Riverwalk
- **Pros:**
  - Suite layout with separate living area and kitchenette
  - Full-size fridge — buy groceries for snacks/breakfasts
  - Free hot breakfast
  - Extra space means kids aren't climbing over everyone
- **Cons:**
  - Slightly further from Riverwalk than the other options
  - Less "hotel experience" — more apartment-style
- **Why it's great for kids:** The suite layout gives parents a moment of sanity after a full day of activities

---

### Austin — 4 Nights (April 13–17)
*Target: Walkable to South Congress (SoCo) and/or downtown*

---

#### Option A: 🥇 Best Location
### **Hotel San José (South Congress)**
- **Price:** ~$180–$240/night → **~$720–$960 for 4 nights**
- **Location:** Right on South Congress Ave — the heart of Austin cool
- **Pros:**
  - Iconic Austin boutique hotel — you're staying IN the experience
  - Walk to restaurants, shops, food trucks, and live music on SoCo
  - Stylish, unique — kids remember it
  - Pool
- **Cons:**
  - Boutique rooms are small — tight for 4 people
  - At the top of your hotel budget
  - Books out fast during Spring Break
- **Best for:** Families who want the full Austin experience and don't mind cozy rooms

---

#### Option B: 💰 Best Value + Space
### **Fairfield Inn & Suites Austin South**
- **Price:** ~$120–$155/night → **~$480–$620 for 4 nights**
- **Location:** South Austin — 10-minute drive or 20-minute walk to SoCo
- **Pros:**
  - Free breakfast (again — huge savings)
  - Suites with sleeper sofa available
  - Free parking (rare in Austin)
  - Pool
  - Reliable, consistent quality
- **Cons:**
  - Not walkable to SoCo without a longer walk
  - Chain hotel feel — less "Austin" personality
- **Best for:** Families prioritizing budget and comfort over location

---

#### Option C: 🎯 Best Middle Ground
### **South Congress Hotel**
- **Price:** ~$160–$210/night → **~$640–$840 for 4 nights**
- **Location:** Directly on South Congress
- **Pros:**
  - Modern boutique feel with larger rooms than Hotel San José
  - Walking distance to everything on SoCo
  - Excellent on-site restaurant (Café No Sé) — convenient for tired evenings
  - Rooftop pool
- **Cons:**
  - Pricier than chain options
  - Valet parking only at ~$35/night
- **Best for:** Families wanting boutique Austin experience with more space than Hotel San José

> **⭐ Austin recommendation:** If budget allows, **South Congress Hotel** for the experience. If watching the budget, **Fairfield Inn & Suites** and use the savings for activities and food trucks.

---

## 3. 📅 Day-by-Day Itinerary

---

### 🌮 SAN ANTONIO (April 10–13)

---

#### **April 10 (Thursday) — Arrival Day**
*You're arriving afternoon — kids are tired, adults are stressed from travel. Keep it easy.*

**Afternoon:**
- Land at SAT, collect bags, pick up rental car (~45–60 min total)
- Check into hotel, dump bags, let everyone reset (30 min)

**Early Evening (~5:30–6:30 PM):**
- Walk to the **Riverwalk** — just walk it. No agenda. Let the kids soak it up
- This is one of those rare urban spaces that genuinely impresses children — the sunken river level, the boats, the lights coming on at dusk
- If staying at Drury, grab their free 5:30 Kickback snacks first

**Dinner:**
- **Casa Rio** on the Riverwalk — one of the oldest restaurants on the river, outdoor seating directly over the water, kid-friendly Mexican food, and colorful boats drift by while you eat. Touristy? Yes. Magical for first-timers? Also yes.
- OR grab **tacos from a nearby spot** and eat at a Riverwalk table if everyone's too tired for a sit-down

**Night:**
- Early bedtime. Tomorrow is a big day.

---

#### **April 11 (Friday) — The Alamo + Theme Park Day**
*Big historic morning, big fun afternoon*

**Morning (9:00 AM):**
- 🏛️ **The Alamo** — Opens at 9 AM; arrive early before Spring Break crowds build
  - Free admission to the church/shrine; small fee for expanded exhibits
  - The 11-year-old will get more out of it; engage the 8-year-old with the "defending the fort" story angle
  - Plan 1–1.5 hours
- Walk Alamo Plaza afterward — street performers, open space for kids to move

**Late Morning → Afternoon:**
- 🎢 **Six Flags Fiesta Texas** OR **SeaWorld San Antonio**
  - Both are ~20 min from downtown
  - **Six Flags** = better roller coasters (the 11-year-old will love Iron Rattler)
  - **SeaWorld** = better for the 8-year-old, animal shows, and it's less crowded than Six Flags on Spring Break
  - **Budget tip:** Buy tickets online in advance — saves $20–$30 per person vs. gate price
  - Plan 4–6 hours
  - Pack snacks — theme park food is expensive

**Evening:**
- Back to hotel, pool time if kids have any energy left
- **Dinner:** Order pizza or hit a nearby casual spot — everyone will be exhausted

---

#### **April 12 (Saturday) — San Antonio Zoo + Pearl District**
*Easier pace than yesterday — San Antonio has more to offer beyond the obvious*

**Morning (9:30 AM):**
- 🦁 **San Antonio Zoo** — Excellent mid-size zoo; kids ages 8 and 11 are exactly the right age
  - Tickets: ~$18–$22/person; buy online
  - Plan 3–4 hours
  - The African exhibits and the new Amazonia section are highlights
  - Get there early — April heat builds by afternoon

**Lunch:**
- **Pearl Brewery District** (~10 min drive) — One of San Antonio's coolest neighborhoods
  - **Weekend Farmers Market at Pearl** (Saturdays 9 AM–1 PM): food stalls, local vendors, tacos, kolaches, fresh juice — perfect family lunch
  - The kids will find food they love; adults will find good coffee

**Afternoon:**
- **San Antonio Museum of Art** (in Pearl area) OR
- **Kiddie Park** — America's oldest children's amusement park, low-key, perfect for the 8-year-old
- OR head back to the **Riverwalk** for a **River Cruise** — 35-minute narrated boat tour, ~$15/person, great for tired legs

**Evening:**
- **Dinner on the Riverwalk** — try **Biga on the Banks** for something more upscale (adults will appreciate it) or **Acenar** for excellent Mexican with a river view
- Evening Riverwalk stroll — it's especially beautiful lit up at night

---

#### **April 13 (Sunday) — Morning Activity + Drive to Austin**
*Checkout, quick activity, hit the road by noon*

**Morning (9:00–11:00 AM):**
- 🦋 **San Antonio Botanical Garden** OR **Natural Bridge Caverns**
  - **Botanical Garden:** Beautiful in April (spring blooms), has a kids' adventure garden, ~$15/adult, $10/child, walkable and calm
  - **Natural Bridge Caverns:** ~30 min north of SA, fascinating cave system kids absolutely love, but plan 2+ hours — better if you leave San Antonio at 10:30
  - *Pick one based on energy level*

**11:30 AM:** Check out of hotel

**Noon:** Grab tacos to go (gas station tacos in San Antonio are legitimately excellent — try **Stripes** or **Bill Miller Bar-B-Q** for a fast Texas BBQ lunch)

**Drive to Austin:**
- Depart San Antonio ~12:00–12:30 PM
- Arrive Austin ~1:30–2:00 PM

---

### 🎸 AUSTIN (April 13–17)

---

#### **April 13 (Sunday) — Arrive Austin, First Taste of SoCo**
*First impressions of Austin should feel fun, not overwhelming*

**Afternoon:**
- Check into hotel (~2:00–3:00 PM)
- **South Congress Avenue Walk** — Just walk SoCo from your hotel
  - Pop into **Uncommon Objects** (weird antique shop kids love)
  - Stop at **Hey Cupcake!** food truck for a snack
  - Let kids browse — it's a highly walkable, stimulating street

**Early Evening:**
- 🍕 **Homeslice Pizza** on SoCo — legendary Austin pizza, great for families, expect a wait but worth it
- OR **Torchy's Tacos** — Austin institution, always kid-approved

**Night:**
- Walk to **Congress Avenue Bridge at dusk** (10-min walk or short drive) — from late March through October, **1.5 million Mexican free-tail bats** emerge at sunset. This is one of the most spectacular free natural shows in the country. The kids will talk about this for years.
  - Arrive 15–30 min before sunset; check exact sunset time
  - It's completely free; stand on the bridge or in the park below

---

#### **April 14 (Monday) — Texas State History + Barton Springs**
*Culture in the morning, outdoor fun in the afternoon*

**Morning (9:30 AM):**
- 🏛️ **Bullock Texas State History Museum**
  - Genuinely excellent museum — three floors of Texas history from indigenous cultures through modern times
  - IMAX theater in the building — check what's playing
  - Tickets: ~$13/adult, $9/child
  - Plan 2–2.5 hours
  - The 11-year-old especially will find the Texas Revolution and oil boom exhibits engaging

**Lunch:**
- **Hopdoddy Burger Bar** (SoCo) — freshly ground burgers, fantastic milkshakes, easy win with kids

**Afternoon:**
- 🏊 **Barton Springs Pool** — A natural spring-fed swimming pool in Zilker Park
  - Water is a constant 68°F year-round — refreshing in April heat
  - $5–$9 per person; one of the great Austin experiences
  - Bring towels, sunscreen, and snacks
  - Plan 2–3 hours

**Evening:**
- Explore **Zilker Park** surrounding the pool — wide open green space, great for running around
- **Dinner:** **Chuy's** on Barton Springs Road — classic Austin Tex-Mex, family-friendly, giant portions, kids' menu

---

#### **April 15 (Tuesday) — Nature + Live Music Introduction**
*Austin's outdoor side + introducing kids to live music culture*

**Morning (9:00 AM):**
- 🦋 **Barton Creek Greenbelt** — Hike one of the easier trails (Barton Creek Trail, ~2 miles)
  - Beautiful limestone canyon, creek swimming holes, native wildflowers in April
  - Free; bring water and snacks
  - Perfect for active 8 and 11-year-olds
  - Plan 2–3 hours

**Lunch:**
- **Picnic at the Greenbelt** (pack it) OR
- **Juan in a Million** on East Cesar Chavez — famous breakfast tacos, cash only, quintessential Austin

**Afternoon:**
- 🦋 **Austin Nature & Science Center** (in Zilker Park)
  - Free/low-cost; excellent for kids — live animals, fossils, nature exhibits
  - Right next to Barton Springs area
  - Plan 1.5 hours
- OR **Thinkery** (children's museum) — hands-on STEM activities; better for the 8-year-old specifically

**Evening:**
- Dinner on **East 6th Street** (the hip, less touristy version of 6th)
- **Rainey Street** for a walk — kid-friendly bungalow bars in early evening (before it becomes a late-night scene)
- After dinner: **6th Street** or **Congress Avenue** — even if you don't go into venues, the energy of live music spilling out of clubs is an experience. The kids will hear 5 different bands just walking two blocks. This IS Austin.

---

#### **April 16 (Wednesday) — Day Trip Option OR Austin Explorer**
*Two options depending on the family's energy level*

**Option A: Day Trip to Enchanted Rock (~1.5 hrs from Austin)**
- 🪨 **Enchanted Rock State Natural Area** — A massive pink granite dome you can hike to the top of
  - Views are spectacular; kids feel like they're on top of the world
  - Moderate hike: ~1 mile round trip to summit
  - **Reserve a day-use pass in advance** at texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com — Enchanted Rock sells out on Spring Break weekends (book as soon as possible)
  - $8/person entry
  - Bring lots of water — it's exposed rock, no shade
  - Full day: leave by 8:30 AM, back by 4–5 PM

**Option B: Stay in Austin**
- Morning: **Texas State Capitol** grounds — free, impressive, kids can do a self-guided tour
- Afternoon: **Blanton Museum of Art** (on UT campus, free on Sundays; Tuesday–Saturday ~$12 adult) OR just walk **UT Austin campus**
- Late afternoon: **Pinballz Arcade** — massive retro arcade, kids go nuts, pay per game or day pass
- Evening: **LAST big dinner in Austin** — make a reservation somewhere special:
  - **Franklin Barbecue** (if you're willing to wait in line 1–2 hours — legendary, bucket-list Texas BBQ)
  - **Terry Black's BBQ** — almost as good as Franklin, no line, more practical for families

---

#### **April 17 (Thursday) — Checkout Morning + Drive to Houston**
*Pack efficiently, one last Austin moment, then hit the road*

**Morning:**
- Grab breakfast tacos from **Veracruz All Natural** (food truck — best breakfast tacos in Austin, fight me)
- Checkout by 11 AM

**Drive Austin → Houston (IAH):**
- Depart Austin ~11:00–11:30 AM
- Arrive IAH ~2:00–2:30 PM (2.5 hrs)
- Drop off rental car, check into airport hotel or explore if time permits

**Optional Houston stop** (if flight is morning April 18):
- Stay near IAH: **Marriott Houston Airport** or **Hyatt Regency Houston Intercontinental** (~$120–$150/night)
- Or if staying near HOU (Hobby): explore **NASA Johnson Space Center** (~$35/adult, $25/child) — 30 min from Hobby, and one of the coolest things your kids will ever see. If you have a free afternoon April 17, this is strongly worth it.

---

## 4. 🎯 Top 5 Must-Do Activities

### San Antonio
1. **The Alamo + Riverwalk** — Non-negotiable; do it your first full morning before crowds
2. **Six Flags Fiesta Texas OR SeaWorld** — The 11-year-old needs a theme park; pick your style
3. **San Antonio Zoo** — Legitimately one of the better mid-size zoos in the country
4. **River Walk Boat Cruise** — 35 minutes, narrated, kids love being on the water
5. **Natural Bridge Caverns** — Stunning cave formations; the "wow factor" for kids is extremely high

### Austin
1. **Congress Avenue Bat Bridge at Sunset** — Free, unforgettable, genuinely one of nature's great spectacles
2. **Barton Springs Pool** — The quintessential Austin outdoor experience; spring-fed, beautiful setting
3. **Bullock Texas State History Museum** — Best museum for kids in Austin; excellent IMAX
4. **South Congress Avenue** — Not just shopping; it IS Austin culture condensed into 10 walkable blocks
5. **Enchanted Rock** OR **Barton Creek Greenbelt** — Pick your nature fix; both are exceptional

---

## 5. 🗺️ Driving Routes

### Route 1: San Antonio (SAT) → Austin
**Distance:** ~80 miles
**Drive Time:** 1 hour 20 min – 1 hour 45 min (without traffic)

**Best Route:** **I-35 North** — direct, straightforward, well-marked

**Traffic Warning:** I-35 through San Marcos and South Austin can slow significantly on Sunday afternoons during Spring Break. Leave San Antonio by noon to avoid the worst of it. Google Maps will reroute you if needed, but there aren't great alternatives — I-35 is the corridor.

**Optional Stop Worth Making:**
- **San Marcos, TX** (~45 min from San Antonio, 45 min from Austin)
  - **Tanger Outlets San Marcos** — Largest outlet center in Texas; great if anyone needs gear or clothing (adults will want to stop, kids may protest)
  - **San Marcos River** — Beautiful spring-fed river; quick stretch stop at City Park
  - **Wonder World Park** — A cave park right in San Marcos; decent alternative to Natural Bridge Caverns if you didn't do that

**Fuel:** Fill up before leaving San Antonio; gas is consistently ~$0.05–$0.15/gallon cheaper in San Antonio than Austin

---

### Route 2: Austin → Houston (IAH or HOU)
**Distance:** ~165 miles to IAH / ~155 miles to HOU (Hobby)
**Drive Time:** 2.5–3 hours (IAH) / 2.5 hours (HOU)

**Best Route to IAH:** **I-10 East** from Austin to Katy, then **I-610 North** to **Beltway 8 (Sam Houston Tollway)** to IAH
- The Sam Houston Tollway segment will charge tolls (~$3–$5) — have cash or a card ready; Texas toll roads accept credit cards

**Best Route to HOU (Hobby):** **TX-71 East** from Austin → **I-10 East** → **Loop 610 South** → HOU
- HOU is significantly closer to downtown Houston and ~20 miles closer to Austin than IAH
- **Strongly consider dropping at HOU** if your airline operates from there — it saves time and the airport is more manageable

**Traffic Warning:** The I-10 corridor west of Houston (Katy Freeway) is one of America's widest highways and can still completely gridlock on weekday afternoons (3–7 PM). **Leaving Austin by 11 AM gives you buffer.**

**Fuel Stops:**
- **Bastrop, TX** (~30 min east of Austin on TX-71) — cheap gas, good stop
- **Columbus, TX** (~90 min from Austin on I-10) — halfway point; good for fuel + a quick stretch

**Interesting Stop (if time permits):**
- **Katy Mills Mall** (just west of Houston) — outlet shopping, massive food court; useful if you have time before the airport
- **George Ranch Historical Park** (~30 min from IAH) — living history museum on a working ranch; niche but fantastic for kids who are into Texas history

## 6. 💰 Budget Breakdown

| Category | Low Estimate | High Estimate | Notes |
|----------|-------------|---------------|-------|
| **Rental Car (7–8 days)** | $420 | $580 | Includes taxes/fees; one-way drop |
| **San Antonio Hotels (3 nights)** | $420 | $660 | Drury Inn (low) to Hyatt Regency (high) |
| **Austin Hotels (4 nights)** | $480 | $960 | Fairfield (low) to South Congress Hotel (high) |
| **Activities** | $280 | $420 | Mix of paid/free; theme park is biggest ticket |
| **Food/Dining** | $480 | $640 | ~$120–$160/day family of 4 |
| **Gas** | $80 | $110 | ~250 total miles; mid-size SUV ~25 mpg |
| **Parking** | $60 | $120 | Hotels + attractions |
| **Miscellaneous/Buffer** | $80 | $130 | Souvenirs, unexpected costs |
| **TOTAL** | **$2,300** | **$3,620** | |

---

### ⚠️ Budget Analysis & Where to Cut

**The honest picture:** At premium hotel choices, this trip easily exceeds $3,000. Here's how to stay under:

#### Non-Negotiable Savings:
1. **Choose Drury Inn in San Antonio** — Free breakfast saves ~$180–$200 over 3 mornings. This single choice gives you significant breathing room.
2. **Choose Fairfield Inn & Suites in Austin** — Free breakfast again; free parking (saves $35/night vs. boutique hotels). Saves $300–$400 vs. South Congress Hotel.
3. **Buy theme park tickets online in advance** — Saves $20–$30/person = $80–$120 for the family

#### If You Pick Budget Hotels AND Free Breakfasts, Your Revised Budget Looks Like:
| Category | Revised Estimate |
|----------|-----------------|
| Rental Car | $480 |
| San Antonio Hotels (Drury Inn) | $450 |
| Austin Hotels (Fairfield) | $520 |
| Activities | $330 |
| Food (no breakfast costs) | $360 |
| Gas + Parking | $160 |
| Miscellaneous | $100 |
| **TOTAL** | **~$2,400** |

**That leaves $600 of cushion** — enough for one splurge dinner, NASA Space Center on the way out, and some souvenir spending.

#### If You Want the Boutique Hotel Experience:
- Cut the theme park (saves ~$200–$250) and substitute the San Antonio Zoo + Riverwalk cruise
- Skip one sit-down restaurant dinner and do food trucks instead (~$40 for the family vs. $120+)
- Pack a cooler with snacks, drinks, and sandwich supplies for driving days — saves $40–$60 per travel day

## 7. 🧰 Practical Tips

### 📱 Best Apps for the Road Trip

| App | Purpose | Notes |
|-----|---------|-------|
| **Google Maps** | Navigation | Download offline maps for Texas before you go |
| **GasBuddy** | Cheapest gas nearby | Texas gas prices vary significantly block to block |
| **Roadtrippers** | Trip planning + points of interest | Good for finding quirky stops kids love |
| **iNaturalist** | Nature identification | Great for Barton Creek Greenbelt — identify plants, birds, bugs with camera |
| **Libby** | Audiobooks + e-books | Free with library card — load up before you leave; great for driving stretches |
| **Kahoot / Heads Up** | Car entertainment | Games kids can play on phones during drives |
| **Waze** | Traffic alerts | Better than Google Maps for real-time congestion warnings on Texas highways |
| **OpenTable / Resy** | Restaurant reservations | Book Austin dinners now — Spring Break fills restaurants fast |

---

### 🎒 What to Pack in the Car

**Essential Car Kit:**
- [ ] Car phone mount (dashboard or vent — you'll use it constantly)
- [ ] USB-C + Lightning charging cables + a multi-port car charger
- [ ] Portable battery pack (kids' phones die at inconvenient times)
- [ ] Reusable water bottles — Texas in April can hit 85°F; hydration matters
- [ ] Small cooler with snacks, fruit, sandwiches, and drinks (cuts food costs significantly)
- [ ] Sunscreen (SPF 50+ — Texas April sun is intense, especially at Enchanted Rock/Barton Springs)
- [ ] Hand sanitizer + small first aid kit
- [ ] Paper towels + small trash bag (car waste is inevitable)

**For the Kids Specifically:**
- [ ] Headphones (individual, not shared — peace in the car)
- [ ] Small backpack each (day pack for activities)
- [ ] Notebook/sketchbook — surprisingly effective car entertainment
- [ ] Motion sickness medication if either child is prone (just in case; I-35 has long flat stretches but city driving can be stop-and-go)

**Clothing Notes for April in Texas:**
- Morning: 60–65°F — light jacket layer
- Afternoon: 78–88°F — shorts and t-shirts
- Rain is possible (April is Texas thunderstorm season) — pack one light rain jacket each
- Comfortable walking shoes are essential — you'll log 4–6 miles/day easily

---

### 📅 April Events & Festivals to Know About

#### San Antonio — April 2025
🎊 **Fiesta San Antonio** — This is massive. Fiesta is a 10-day citywide festival that typically runs mid-to-late April. **Check the exact 2025 dates** at fiesta-sa.org — if any of April 10–13 overlaps with Fiesta, this transforms San Antonio completely.
- Battle of Flowers Parade, Fiesta Flambeau (night parade), food everywhere
- **Upside:** Incredible atmosphere, food stalls, cultural events — kids love it
- **Downside:** Hotel prices spike 20–40%; Riverwalk crowds are intense; book hotels now if Fiesta overlaps your dates

#### Austin — April 2025
- **Austin Food & Wine Festival** — Typically late April; check if it overlaps. If it does, food truck and restaurant waits will be longer downtown
- **UT Spring Events** — Campus will be active; adds energy to the area but also traffic
- **Keep Austin Weird Fest** — Annual festival celebrating Austin's eccentricity; check dates
- **General Spring Break Note:** Austin sees massive tourist influx during spring break season (multiple universities' breaks stagger through March–April). Expect higher restaurant wait times and busier attractions mid-week

> **Action Item:** Check the **2025 Fiesta San Antonio dates** immediately. If it overlaps April 10–13, either lean into it joyfully or reconsider your hotel (book now regardless).

---

### 🏁 Final Pre-Trip Checklist

- [ ] Book rental car NOW (Spring Break inventory disappears fast)
- [ ] Book hotels NOW (especially if Fiesta SA overlaps)
- [ ] Reserve Enchanted Rock day-use pass at texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com
- [ ] Buy theme park tickets online (Six Flags or SeaWorld)
- [ ] Make Austin dinner reservations (at least 2 evenings — Homeslice and one BBQ spot)
- [ ] Download Google Maps Texas offline
- [ ] Confirm credit card rental car insurance coverage (call your card issuer)
- [ ] Check sunset times for Congress Avenue Bat Bridge viewing (April 13–16 window)
- [ ] Verify Drury Inn or chosen hotel's parking situation and rates

---

*Safe travels and happy trails! Texas in April is genuinely spectacular — the wildflowers are out, the weather is perfect for outdoor activities, and the food will make your flight home feel like a cruel punishment. Your kids are at exactly the right age to remember this trip forever.* 🤠
